subject: art-design
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Impressionism is best known for...
options: Capturing fleeting light and everyday scenes with loose brushwork
questions.explain: Impressionists used loose, visible brushstrokes to capture changing light and ordinary moments.

questions.q: Corrugated card is useful in 3D work because it is...
options: Lightweight, strong and easy to score and fold
questions.explain: Corrugated card is light yet rigid, and can be scored and folded to build 3D forms.

questions.q: Expressionism aims above all to convey...
options: The artist's inner emotion and feeling
questions.explain: Expressionism distorts colour and form to express the artist's emotional response rather than reality.

questions.q: A wide aperture (low f-number) produces what kind of depth of field?
options: A shallow depth of field with a blurred background
Total blur across the whole image
A deep depth of field with everything sharp
questions.explain: A wide aperture gives a shallow depth of field, keeping the subject sharp while blurring the background.

questions.q: Which is an example of three-dimensional design in everyday life?
options: A product such as a chair
questions.explain: Product design, such as a chair, is a form of three-dimensional design.

questions.q: Oil paint is mixed and thinned using...
options: Solvents such as turpentine or linseed oil
questions.explain: Oil paint is oil-based and is thinned and cleaned with solvents like turpentine, not water.

questions.q: Which paint is water-based and dries quickly to a permanent finish?
questions.explain: Acrylic paint is water-based, dries fast and becomes water-resistant once dry.

questions.q: Quilting involves...
options: Stitching layers of fabric together, often with wadding between them
questions.explain: Quilting sews together layers of cloth, usually with a padded wadding sandwiched between them.

questions.q: In 3D work, 'armature' refers to...
options: An internal supporting framework for a sculpture
questions.explain: An armature is the internal skeleton, often wire, that supports a modelled sculpture.

questions.q: A 'wordmark' (logotype) is a logo made from...
options: A stylised version of the brand's name in text
questions.explain: A wordmark is a logo formed from the company name set in distinctive, designed lettering.

questions.q: In a mono-print, how many prints can usually be taken from one inking?
questions.explain: A mono-print produces a single, unique image, unlike editions made from a fixed block or plate.

questions.q: Which drawing medium is best for soft, smudgeable, very dark marks?
questions.explain: Charcoal produces rich, dark, easily smudged marks ideal for tonal drawing.

questions.q: What does ISO measure on a camera?
questions.explain: ISO sets the sensor's sensitivity to light; a high ISO brightens images but can add noise.

questions.q: Vincent van Gogh is associated with which movement, known for expressive colour and brushwork?
questions.explain: Van Gogh was a Post-Impressionist, using bold colour and energetic brushstrokes to convey emotion.

questions.q: A 'still life' photograph typically shows...
questions.explain: Still life depicts a deliberate arrangement of inanimate objects, such as fruit or bottles.

questions.q: Which printmaking process is described as 'intaglio', where ink is held in lines cut below the surface?
questions.explain: Etching is an intaglio process: ink sits in the recessed bitten lines, not on the raised surface.

questions.q: What does 'composition' mean in art?
options: The arrangement of elements within an artwork
The size of the canvas only
questions.explain: Composition is how the visual elements are arranged and organised within the picture area.

questions.q: A 'mordant' is used in dyeing to...
options: Help the dye bond permanently to the fibre
questions.explain: A mordant fixes dye to the fibres so the colour is more permanent and less likely to wash out.

questions.q: In a landscape, objects placed at the bottom of the picture usually appear to be in the...
questions.explain: Objects lower in the picture plane normally read as nearer to the viewer, in the foreground.

questions.q: What is the key difference between shape and form?
options: Shape is large, form is small
Shape is coloured, form is not
Shape is two-dimensional, form is three-dimensional
questions.explain: A shape is flat and two-dimensional, while a form has depth and appears three-dimensional.

questions.q: What is the secondary colour made by mixing blue and yellow?
questions.explain: Blue mixed with yellow produces the secondary colour green.

questions.q: A 'mock-up' in graphic design is...
options: A finished printed product for sale
A trial version showing how a design will look
questions.explain: A mock-up is a realistic preview that shows how the final design will appear before production.
